findings.issue_text: `<%- end if %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 is a Ruby syntax error — ERB emits `end if` with no condition into the compiled template, so the first embed/best request for a URL with a topic raises ActionView::Template::Error and 500s on every request; fix is `<%- end %>`

Imported RSS content is stored and rendered completely unsanitized, enabling stored XSS on the forum's own origin — poll_feed.rb passes raw feed content (with CGI.unescapeHTML even re-materializing entity-escaped tags) to TopicEmbed which creates posts with cook_method: raw_html, and the embed view renders it via `raw post.cooked` with no tag/attribute filtering on the RSS path

A single feed item missing `content` (or `title`) crashes the whole import loop in poll_feed.rb:32 — SimpleRSS returns nil for absent elements so `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError, aborting the loop so all subsequent items are never imported, and `retry: false` means the same items are skipped forever on the hourly run

Protocol-relative URLs are mangled into broken host-relative URLs in topic_embed.rb:63-64 and 69-70 — `href.start_with?('/')` matches URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.jpg` and `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both leading slashes, producing broken links like `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/img.jpg`; relative URLs without a leading slash are also left resolving against the forum instead of the source article

TopicEmbed rows are never cleaned up when the topic/post is deleted (no dependent: :destroy or destroy-path cleanup) — topic_id_for_embed keeps returning dead topic ids causing permanent 500s on the embed for that URL, and the next feed poll takes the update path with embed.post == nil leading to PostRevisor.new(nil) → NoMethodError that kills the poll job and blocks all subsequent feed imports

The unauthenticated /embed/best endpoint (embed_controller.rb:15) drives unbounded outbound fetches and topic creation — the only throttle is per-URL (60s), with no per-IP/global rate limit, so an attacker or crawler hitting distinct paths can flood the job queue with synchronous HTTP fetches and pollute the forum with garbage topics created from arbitrary 200-returning pages

`setnx`/`expire` are not atomic in topic_retriever.rb:27-28 — if the process dies between the two calls, the `retrieved:<url>` key persists with no TTL, permanently throttling that URL so every subsequent embed view skips retrieval and shows 'Loading Discussion...' indefinitely with no recovery short of manual Redis cleanup

embed_url is matched as an exact string with no normalization in topic_embed.rb:15,77 — trivial differences between the feed's link and the page's discourseEmbedUrl (trailing slash, http vs https, query params) cause topic_id_for_embed and the existence check to miss, so fetch_http imports the same article twice, creating two topics with split comment threads

`open(url)` in topic_embed.rb:48 is called without `require 'open-uri'` anywhere on the retrieve_topic → topic_retriever → topic_embed code path — in a process that hasn't loaded open-uri, Kernel#open treats the URL as a filename and raises Errno::ENOENT, so retrieval always fails in that process

`String#scrub` in poll_feed.rb:32 requires Ruby ≥ 2.1 — on the Ruby 2.0 current at the PR's date, `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError on every run, making feed importing completely non-functional while CI stays green because the specs stub out poll_feed

Public embed endpoint (embed_controller.rb:15) enqueues background jobs with no request-level rate limit; every miss triggers a remote fetch and permanent topic creation, with only a bypassable 60-second per-URL Redis throttle, a trivially spoofable Referer check, and the loading view reloading every 30s causing ~2 enqueues/minute per visitor forever for unresolvable URLs

A single embed request synchronously runs the entire feed poll (topic_retriever.rb:36): Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) re-downloads and re-parses the whole RSS/Atom feed and re-imports every item (per-item DB lookup, SHA1, possible PostRevisor/PostCreator runs) just to resolve one URL, duplicating the hourly schedule; the unused feed_key (poll_feed.rb:20-22) suggests conditional fetching was intended but never wired up

import_remote (topic_embed.rb:47-48) downloads and parses remote documents with no size limit or explicit timeouts: open(url).read buffers the entire response body in memory, then Readability::Document and Nokogiri make full-document passes, so a large or slow-drip URL pins a Sidekiq worker and spikes memory/CPU; same unguarded open() pattern at poll_feed.rb:29

Feed poll (poll_feed.rb:31-37) iterates all feed items with no cap and a per-item query (N+1 shape): each iteration issues TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first plus a SHA1 over full content and a Nokogiri parse, with no limit on item count and no conditional fetch

best: 5 passed to TopicView (embed_controller.rb:13) may be a no-op: the diff contains no TopicView changes implementing a best option and the spec mocks TopicView.new, so @topic_view.posts may be the full post list, causing the embed view (best.html.erb:12-22) to render every post in the topic with unbounded response size and render cost

Stored, unsanitized HTML: Post#cook returns raw unfiltered for raw_html posts (app/models/post.rb:~133), the feed path stores i.content with no whitelist at all (poll_feed.rb:35, where CGI.unescapeHTML re-materializes escaped HTML), and it is rendered via raw post.cooked (best.html.erb:19), so a malicious or compromised feed source becomes stored HTML served from the Discourse origin

force: true added to an already-shipped migration (db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3) drops an existing top_topics table if the migration is ever (re-)evaluated against a DB that has it — a data-loss hazard pattern in a released migration

Stored XSS: external feed content is imported and served as raw HTML with zero sanitization — the new raw_html cook method makes Post#cook return raw verbatim bypassing the Sanitize pipeline, the RSS path feeds CGI.unescapeHTML-decoded payloads into TopicEmbed.import, absolutize_urls' Nokogiri round-trip preserves script/onerror markup, and TopicEmbed.import interpolates the feed-controlled url into href with only a ^https?:// prefix regex check, so hostile feed content executes for forum users and visitors of third-party embedding pages

New embed asset manifests (embed.css.scss, embed.js) are never registered in config.assets.precompile — the embed layout references stylesheet_link_tag 'embed' but under Rails 4/sprockets-rails 2 production defaults every /embed/best request would 500, and embed.js has no route, precompile entry, or stable URL for external consumption

Breaking CLI contract change: the --category/-c thor option was removed from the Disqus importer, so existing invocations passing -c fail on Thor's unknown-option check and imported topics silently lose category assignment and original created_at preservation; the importer also switched to live-fetching thread URLs via TopicEmbed.import_remote, silently skipping dead or non-http links instead of importing them

Anonymous users can make the forum scrape and publish arbitrary pages of the embeddable host — the embed controller enqueues retrieve_topic with a fully user-controlled embed_url before any validation, and the job only checks URI(embed_url).host == embeddable_host leaving the path unrestricted, bypassing all posting permissions/trust levels by publishing as the configured embed_by_username user; the 60s throttle is per-URL so unlimited distinct URLs also flood sidekiq and hammer the host

absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs: //cdn.example.com/img.png matches start_with?('/'), gets its leading slashes stripped and is prefixed with the embed host producing http://blog.example.com/cdn.example.com/img.png; plain relative URLs (foo.html) are also left un-absolutized and break in the embedded context despite the method's stated contract

Embed resolution requires byte-exact match between the page URL and the feed link — topic_id_for_embed does exact string matching between the embed_url query param and the stored embed_url, so any divergence (trailing slash, scheme, or query params like FeedBurner's utm_source=feedburner) means the embed never resolves and the iframe shows the loading page forever, reloading every 30s and re-enqueueing retrieval every 60s with no error surfaced

One malformed feed item permanently wedges the hourly feed import — rss.items.each calls TopicEmbed.import with no per-item error handling and the job sets retry: false, so a single item with nil title/content, a duplicate link (unique index on embed_url causing RecordNotUnique), or any import exception aborts the loop and every subsequent hourly run crashes at the same item, silently skipping everything after it forever

content_sha1 is advanced even when the revision didn't apply — embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...) runs regardless of whether revise! actually revised (it can return false or be aborted by a before_save callback), so once the sha1 is advanced changed content is never re-imported on later polls; the bypass_rate_limiter: true opt passed to PostRevisor has no corresponding handling in the code and is silently ignored

embed.js postMessage origin check is substring-prefix based — discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 accepts any origin that is a string prefix of the forum URL (e.g., a forum at http://discourse.example.com accepts messages from http://discourse.example.co), enabling iframe-height manipulation as a clickjacking assist; the check should compare e.origin against the forum's exact origin

force: true in create_table migrations silently drops an existing table and its data if the migration executes where the table already exists, and retroactively editing the already-released create_top_topics migration has no effect on databases that already applied it, diverging schema.rb-vs-migrations environments

Referer header is the only authorization gate for the embed endpoint — browsers/privacy settings that suppress Referer produce URI('').host == nil leading to a 403, so the embed silently never loads for those visitors with no fallback (e.g., signed/tokenized embed URL) and an invisible failure mode for both the embedding site and the forum operator

Stored XSS: the raw_html cook method makes cooked byte-identical to unsanitized raw, which Discourse renders with raw everywhere (embed view and normal topic views); feed item content never passes through any sanitizer and poll_feed.rb even calls CGI.unescapeHTML, converting entity-escaped <script> tags in feeds back into live tags, so a malicious/compromised feed or embeddable host yields stored XSS executing for every viewer including staff

<%- end if %> in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 is invalid ERB — Rails' erubis compiler emits 'end if ;' which is a Ruby syntax error, so the template fails to compile and every embed/best request that finds a topic returns 500; only the loading path works, and controller specs don't render views so tests won't catch it

Unescaped request.referer is interpolated into an inline JavaScript string in app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — the ensure_embeddable host check constrains only the host, not path/query, so a crafted URL on an embeddable host breaks out of the JS string causing XSS on the Discourse origin with the viewer's cookies in scope; needs j/JSON encoding

External fetches have no timeout, size limit, or error handling — open-uri defaults in poll_feed.rb and topic_embed.rb leave ~60s+ per socket operation and unbounded read body size, so a slow or huge feed/page blocks Sidekiq workers for minutes or exhausts memory, and any SocketError/Timeout/parse error propagates as an unhandled job failure

Throttle key is acquired before the fetch in lib/topic_retriever.rb — retrieved_recently? sets the 60s redis key before perform_retrieve runs, so if the fetch fails the job's first Sidekiq retry lands inside the throttle window, does nothing, and 'succeeds', ending the retry chain; transient failures are never effectively retried and recovery depends on new pageviews after 60s

Every retrieval synchronously re-polls the entire feed — Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) runs the full feed fetch and import inline inside the retrieve_topic job, so any exception while polling propagates and skips fetch_http, meaning one broken feed item breaks on-demand embedding for every URL site-wide and is re-attempted on each job retry

No nil/validation guards on feed items in poll_feed.rb — i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError when an item lacks content, a nil i.title blows up topic creation, and URI(url) in TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls raises on feeds with unencoded spaces in links; the exception aborts the items loop and with retry: false a single persistent malformed item permanently blocks import of every item after it in the feed

TopicEmbed rows are never cleaned up when topics/posts are deleted (no dependent/destroy hooks) — a stale row makes topic_id_for_embed return a dead id so TopicView.new raises, causing permanent 404/500 for that embed URL with no re-enqueued retrieval, and the update path crashes on PostRevisor.new(nil) when embed.post is nil

Unauthenticated embed endpoint enqueues a background job per request with no throttle or input cap — the Referer check is trivially forged, there is no per-IP/route rate limit, no dedup, and no length limit on the embed_url param (job args go straight into redis), so combined with the 30s reload loop in loading.html.erb this is a Sidekiq/redis flooding vector

String#scrub requires Ruby 2.1+ but Ruby 2.0 was in use at the time and the string-scrub backport is not bundled in this PR — calling it in poll_feed.rb would be a NoMethodError breaking all feed polling

Non-atomic setnx/expire throttle in lib/topic_retriever.rb — if the process dies between setnx and expire the key has no TTL and that embed URL is permanently throttled (never retrieved again); should be a single SET with EX/NX

force: true in create_table migrations (create_topic_embeds.rb and the edit to already-shipped create_top_topics.rb) silently DROPs the table and its data if it already exists, and editing an already-released migration means existing installs never see the change

Silent failure paths with no logging anywhere in the pipeline — topic_retriever.rb silently returns when the embed_by_username user is missing and topic_embed.rb silently returns for non-http URLs, so when embedding doesn't work jobs 'succeed' while doing nothing with no log or error to diagnose it

Referer-based gating breaks for referer-suppressing clients — browsers/privacy settings/referrerpolicy that omit the Referer fail the host check and get 403 forever with no fallback, so the embed silently never loads for those users

app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 closes the header conditional with `<%- end if %>`, which ERB compiles to the Ruby statement `end if` — a syntax error (it should be `<%- end %>`); every request to /embed/best for a topic with posts raises ActionView::Template::Error and returns a 500.

The embed templates (best.html.erb, loading.html.erb, and the embed layout including the postMessage height reporting) are executed by zero tests: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:48-52 mocks TopicView entirely (returning nil) and the controller specs lack render_views, so templates are never compiled; even adding render_views would not help since the TopicView mock returns nil and the template would crash on @topic_view.posts.

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:40-46 uses TopicRetriever.expects(:new) with no with(...), so the controller→job→retriever argument passing (embed_url, user_id) is completely unpinned.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:24-38 — poll_feed's actual behavior has zero coverage: no test parses a feed, exercises CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub), the link→id fallback, or the per-item TopicEmbed.import.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:56-77 — absolutize_urls mishandles protocol-relative URLs: '//cdn.example.com/a.png' matches start_with?('/') and then has all leading slashes stripped by sub(/^\/+/, ''), producing http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/a.png — silently broken images/links.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:56-77 — absolutize_urls edge cases are untested: non-standard ports and the 'already-absolute URLs stay untouched' invariant are unpinned.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17-19 — the postMessage origin check and the resize handler have no JS test coverage.

Poison-item cascade in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:27-33`: `rss.items.each` has no per-item error handling, so any exception aborts the run mid-iteration — e.g. nil `i.content` (SimpleRSS exposes `content:encoded` underscored) causing `nil.scrub` NoMethodError, a stale embed whose post was deleted crashing `PostRevisor.new(nil)` at `topic_embed.rb:30`, or `URI()` raising inside `absolutize_urls`; with `sidekiq_options retry: false` the next hourly run dies at the same item, permanently and silently halting all feed importing, and `topic_retriever.rb:37` invoking `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously per embed request compounds the failure

`cook_method` is settable through `PostCreator` opts (`lib/post_creator.rb:216`) with no allow-list of callers — a mass-assignment escape hatch to the unsanitized-HTML path; if any controller passes request params through as opts, any user can post with `cook_method=2` and store arbitrary raw HTML (trivial stored XSS), so the knob must be restricted to internal importers

Host validation is scheme/port-blind and redirect-blind, enabling SSRF probing from the Discourse server (`lib/topic_retriever.rb:15`, `app/models/topic_embed.rb:42`): `invalid_host?` compares only `URI(@embed_url).host`, so `http://<embeddable_host>:6379/` and `ftp://` URLs pass the guard and are fetched by `open(url)` (open-uri supports FTP; the `^https?://` check in `import` runs only after the fetch), and open-uri following redirects lets an open redirect on the embeddable host make the server fetch internal/metadata URLs whose content is stored and readable back via the embed endpoint

Unauthenticated, unthrottled Sidekiq job enqueue (queue-flooding DoS) at `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15`: the only gate on `GET /embed/best` is the client-controlled, trivially spoofable `Referer` header, and the 60s throttle lives inside the job, so every request with an unknown `embed_url` enqueues a `retrieve_topic` job plus a DB lookup at unbounded rate, flooding the shared Sidekiq queue and delaying legitimate work site-wide

Exact-string URL keying with no normalization (`app/models/topic_embed.rb:11, 71`, `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:10`): `embed_url` is matched by exact string equality everywhere (lookup, unique index, throttle key), so trailing-slash, scheme (http/https), `www`, or query-param (`utm_*`) differences between the feed's `link` and the page's `discourseEmbedUrl` produce duplicate topics/discussions or a lookup that never hits, leaving the client reloading `loading.html.erb` every 30s forever while jobs keep being enqueued

Stale `TopicEmbed` rows after topic/post deletion (`app/models/topic_embed.rb:27-31, 71`): there is no `dependent: :destroy` between Topic/Post and TopicEmbed, so deleting an imported topic leaves the row — `topic_id_for_embed` returns a dead id, `TopicView.new` raises RecordNotFound, and that URL's embed 404s forever with no recovery path; the update path also calls `PostRevisor.new(embed.post)` on a nil post, causing a NoMethodError that feeds the poller cascade

`absolutize_urls` corrupts protocol-relative URLs (`app/models/topic_embed.rb:58-59`, same pattern for `img` at ~63-64): `href.start_with?('/')` matches `//cdn.example.com/x`, then `sub(/^\+/, '')` strips both slashes, producing a broken host-relative URL like `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/x` for every protocol-relative link/image in imported content

`setnx`/`expire` in `lib/topic_retriever.rb:25-26` are not atomic: a crash between them leaves a TTL-less `retrieved:<url>` key, so that URL is considered 'recently retrieved' forever and is never imported (stuck on loading); should use a single atomic SET with EX

No terminal failure state and silent failures (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:8-10`, `lib/topic_retriever.rb:45-46`): the loading view reloads every 30s indefinitely, `fetch_http` silently returns when the `embed_by_username` user is missing, and failed fetches (404 page, blocked UA, empty readability result) are never logged or surfaced — misconfigured instances show an infinite 'Loading Discussion…' with zero diagnostics

`force: true` in `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:4` silently drops any pre-existing table if the migration is re-run (redo, out-of-sync `schema_migrations`), and editing the already-released `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:2` means DBs that ran the original never see the change and diverge from fresh installs

`<%- end if %>` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6` works only by accident: ERB compiles it to `end if`, which Ruby parses as a modifier-if whose condition is the next statement Erubis emits (always truthy), so it renders correctly today purely by that accident — any adjacent template edit or different ERB compiler silently changes the condition or breaks compilation; should be `<%- end %>`

`disqus.thor` behavior regressions (`lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117-146`): the `category` and `created_at` options were removed so imported topics lose category and original timestamps, threads whose links aren't http(s) or whose live fetch fails are now silently skipped where they previously always imported, and `import_remote` makes a live HTTP request per thread

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

Imported RSS content is stored and rendered completely unsanitized, enabling stored XSS on the forum's own origin — poll_feed.rb passes raw feed content (with CGI.unescapeHTML even re-materializing entity-escaped tags) to TopicEmbed which creates posts with cook_method: raw_html, and the embed view renders it via `raw post.cooked` with no tag/attribute filtering on the RSS path

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an RSS import path that bypasses Discourse’s normal cooking/sanitization. `Jobs::PollFeed` takes feed item HTML (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`, and `Post#cook` explicitly returns `raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`, skipping the rendering pipeline. The embed view then renders the result with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. On the RSS path there is no tag/attribute sanitization (unlike `import_remote`, which restricts tags/attributes via ruby-readability), so malicious feed HTML could be stored and served from the forum origin, enabling stored XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: A single feed item missing `content` (or `title`) crashes the whole import loop in poll_feed.rb:32 — SimpleRSS returns nil for absent elements so `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError, aborting the loop so all subsequent items are never imported, and `retry: false` means the same items are skipped forever on the hourly run

Protocol-relative URLs are mangled into broken host-relative URLs in topic_embed.rb:63-64 and 69-70 — `href.start_with?('/')` matches URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.jpg` and `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both leading slashes, producing broken links like `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/img.jpg`; relative URLs without a leading slash are also left resolving against the forum instead of the source article

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` (new file), both link and image rewriting only check `start_with?('/')` and then do `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"` / same for `src`. This will also match protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x.png`; `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both leading slashes, producing `http://<source-host>/cdn.example.com/x.png`, which is incorrect. Additionally, relative URLs without a leading slash (e.g. `images/x.png` or `../x`) are not rewritten at all, so they will resolve relative to the Discourse embed page rather than the source article URL when rendered, breaking imported content. This is a concrete, diff-grounded behavior defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed rows are never cleaned up when the topic/post is deleted (no dependent: :destroy or destroy-path cleanup) — topic_id_for_embed keeps returning dead topic ids causing permanent 500s on the embed for that URL, and the next feed poll takes the update path with embed.post == nil leading to PostRevisor.new(nil) → NoMethodError that kills the poll job and blocks all subsequent feed imports

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `TopicEmbed` is introduced with `belongs_to :topic` and `belongs_to :post` but no `dependent: :destroy` on the owning models (and no other cleanup path shown). `topic_id_for_embed` (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url).pluck(:topic_id).first`) will continue returning a `topic_id` even if the referenced topic is deleted, and `EmbedController#best` will then call `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` without verifying the topic still exists. Separately, in `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then (when content changes) calls `PostRevisor.new(post)`; if the post was deleted, `embed.post` will be `nil`, making `PostRevisor.new(nil)` a likely runtime error. These are concrete failure modes directly implied by the new code and lack of lifecycle cleanup/null checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The unauthenticated /embed/best endpoint (embed_controller.rb:15) drives unbounded outbound fetches and topic creation — the only throttle is per-URL (60s), with no per-IP/global rate limit, so an attacker or crawler hitting distinct paths can flood the job queue with synchronous HTTP fetches and pollute the forum with garbage topics created from arbitrary 200-returning pages

adjudication.rationale: The new unauthenticated `GET /embed/best` route enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, embed_url: ...)` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` is nil (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). The job calls `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, whose only rate limiting is a Redis throttle keyed by the full `@embed_url` for 60s (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), i.e., per-URL only (lib/topic_retriever.rb). An attacker can vary `embed_url` paths on the allowed host to enqueue many jobs and trigger many HTTP fetches (`TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses `open(url).read`) and topic/post creation (`TopicEmbed.import` creates via `PostCreator` with `skip_validations: true`). There is no per-IP, per-host, or global enqueue limit/deduplication shown in the diff; `ensure_embeddable` only checks `request.referer` host against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, which can be spoofed and does not mitigate volume.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `setnx`/`expire` are not atomic in topic_retriever.rb:27-28 — if the process dies between the two calls, the `retrieved:<url>` key persists with no TTL, permanently throttling that URL so every subsequent embed view skips retrieval and shows 'Loading Discussion...' indefinitely with no recovery short of manual Redis cleanup

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently? the throttle key is set with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then TTL is applied in a separate call `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process/job crashes or is killed after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will persist without a TTL, making `retrieved_recently?` return true forever for that embed_url and preventing `perform_retrieve` from ever running again. Given EmbedController#best renders `loading` when no TopicEmbed exists and relies on the async job to retrieve, this can lead to permanent "Loading Discussion..." until manual Redis cleanup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_url is matched as an exact string with no normalization in topic_embed.rb:15,77 — trivial differences between the feed's link and the page's discourseEmbedUrl (trailing slash, http vs https, query params) cause topic_id_for_embed and the existence check to miss, so fetch_http imports the same article twice, creating two topics with split comment threads

adjudication.rationale: The diff stores and looks up TopicEmbed records by exact `embed_url` string equality (e.g., `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` in `TopicEmbed.import`, `topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` uses `where(embed_url: embed_url)`, and `TopicRetriever` checks `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`). There is no canonicalization/normalization of URLs (scheme, trailing slash, query params, etc.). Given this, two semantically-identical URLs that differ trivially will be treated as distinct and can result in multiple imports/topics for the same article, splitting comment threads—especially since imports can occur from both RSS (`PollFeed`) and direct HTTP fetch (`import_remote`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `open(url)` in topic_embed.rb:48 is called without `require 'open-uri'` anywhere on the retrieve_topic → topic_retriever → topic_embed code path — in a process that hasn't loaded open-uri, Kernel#open treats the URL as a filename and raises Errno::ENOENT, so retrieval always fails in that process

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote` the code calls `open(url).read` (topic_embed.rb) but this file (and the shown `retrieve_topic` → `TopicRetriever` path) does not `require 'open-uri'`. The only added `require 'open-uri'` in the diff is inside `Jobs::PollFeed`, which is a different code path. Without `open-uri`, `Kernel#open` will treat the URL as a local filename and can raise `Errno::ENOENT`, breaking remote retrieval via `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` / `TopicEmbed.import_remote` in processes that haven’t already loaded open-uri.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `String#scrub` in poll_feed.rb:32 requires Ruby ≥ 2.1 — on the Ruby 2.0 current at the PR's date, `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError on every run, making feed importing completely non-functional while CI stays green because the specs stub out poll_feed

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Jobs::PollFeed` and it calls `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). That is a concrete compatibility risk because `String#scrub` is not guaranteed to exist on older Ruby versions, and the new specs for `PollFeed` only assert whether `poll_feed` is invoked but never execute `poll_feed`/parse RSS content, so CI would not catch a runtime `NoMethodError` from this line. However, the diff alone does not state the project’s required Ruby version, so it’s not fully verifiable as a definite break in this repo.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public embed endpoint (embed_controller.rb:15) enqueues background jobs with no request-level rate limit; every miss triggers a remote fetch and permanent topic creation, with only a bypassable 60-second per-URL Redis throttle, a trivially spoofable Referer check, and the loading view reloading every 30s causing ~2 enqueues/minute per visitor forever for unresolvable URLs

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil it unconditionally enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). The `loading` template auto-reloads every 30s (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb), which will repeatedly hit the endpoint and enqueue again for unresolved URLs. The only throttling shown is inside `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` (lib/topic_retriever.rb), which is per-URL and happens after the job is already enqueued (so it doesn’t protect the request/job queue), and can be bypassed by varying `embed_url`. The embeddable check relies on `request.referer` host equality (ensure_embeddable), which is a client-controlled header and thus not a robust gate. This combination is a verifiable abuse/DoS vector introduced by the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` synchronously calling `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true (lib/topic_retriever.rb). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` downloads/parses the feed (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`) and iterates every item, calling `TopicEmbed.import` for each (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), which can perform per-item DB lookups and potentially create/revise posts. This is a concrete performance/architecture concern on a single embed request and duplicates the hourly scheduled poll behavior. Also, `feed_key` is defined but never used (poll_feed.rb), supporting the finding that conditional/etag-based fetching may have been intended but not wired.

adjudication_records.issue_text: import_remote (topic_embed.rb:47-48) downloads and parses remote documents with no size limit or explicit timeouts: open(url).read buffers the entire response body in memory, then Readability::Document and Nokogiri make full-document passes, so a large or slow-drip URL pins a Sidekiq worker and spikes memory/CPU; same unguarded open() pattern at poll_feed.rb:29

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces unbounded remote fetches using Ruby open-uri without explicit timeouts or size limits: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` and then runs `Readability::Document`/`Nokogiri` over the full document, and `Jobs::PollFeed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`. Both are executed in background jobs (`RetrieveTopic`/`TopicRetriever` and `PollFeed`), so a large response or slow-drip server can tie up a Sidekiq worker and cause excessive memory/CPU usage. This availability/resource-exhaustion risk is directly verifiable from the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Feed poll (poll_feed.rb:31-37) iterates all feed items with no cap and a per-item query (N+1 shape): each iteration issues TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first plus a SHA1 over full content and a Nokogiri parse, with no limit on item count and no conditional fetch

For each item it calls `TopicEmbed.import(...)`, which performs a per-item DB lookup (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`) and additional per-item work (SHA1 of full contents and `Nokogiri::HTML.fragment` via `absolutize_urls`). This is a concrete perf/scalability concern introduced by the diff, but not a correctness/security defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored, unsanitized HTML: Post#cook returns raw unfiltered for raw_html posts (app/models/post.rb:~133), the feed path stores i.content with no whitelist at all (poll_feed.rb:35, where CGI.unescapeHTML re-materializes escaped HTML), and it is rendered via raw post.cooked (best.html.erb:19), so a malicious or compromised feed source becomes stored HTML served from the Discourse origin

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a raw-HTML rendering path where imported content bypasses Discourse’s normal cooking/sanitization. `Post#cook` now returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb), and `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` using `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). Feed polling pulls `i.content` and runs `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) without any sanitization/whitelist, and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). This combination makes stored, unfiltered HTML from a feed/remote source renderable from the Discourse origin, enabling stored XSS if the source is malicious/compromised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true added to an already-shipped migration (db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3) drops an existing top_topics table if the migration is ever (re-)evaluated against a DB that has it — a data-loss hazard pattern in a released migration

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists before recreating it, so if this migration is ever run against a DB that already has `top_topics` (e.g., schema_migrations mismatch, reset/rollback+re-run scenarios), it can destroy existing data in that table.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: external feed content is imported and served as raw HTML with zero sanitization — the new raw_html cook method makes Post#cook return raw verbatim bypassing the Sanitize pipeline, the RSS path feeds CGI.unescapeHTML-decoded payloads into TopicEmbed.import, absolutize_urls' Nokogiri round-trip preserves script/onerror markup, and TopicEmbed.import interpolates the feed-controlled url into href with only a ^https?:// prefix regex check, so hostile feed content executes for forum users and visitors of third-party embedding pages

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `raw_html` cook method (`Post.cook_methods`) and makes `Post#cook` return `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == :raw_html` (bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and feeds it HTML pulled from RSS (`Jobs::PollFeed` uses `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) or from `Readability::Document` (`TopicEmbed.import_remote`). `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative `href/src` and does not sanitize/strip scripts or event handlers; it round-trips through Nokogiri and returns `fragment.to_html`. Additionally, `import` interpolates the feed-controlled `url` into an `<a href='#{url}'>` string with only a `^https?://` prefix regex guard, so quotes/attribute injection is possible. The embed view renders `raw post.cooked`, which under `raw_html` is unescaped attacker-controlled HTML. This is a verifiable stored XSS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New embed asset manifests (embed.css.scss, embed.js) are never registered in config.assets.precompile — the embed layout references stylesheet_link_tag 'embed' but under Rails 4/sprockets-rails 2 production defaults every /embed/best request would 500, and embed.js has no route, precompile entry, or stable URL for external consumption

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds standalone assets `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss` and `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`. The new layout `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb` calls `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'`, but the diff does not show `embed.css` being pulled in via an existing manifest (e.g. `application.css`) or being added to an assets precompile list. Under typical Rails 4 production settings (`config.assets.compile = false`), referencing a non-precompiled asset via `stylesheet_link_tag` can raise `AssetNotPrecompiledError` (500). Similarly, `embed.js` is introduced but not referenced anywhere in the app and is not shown being precompiled or exposed for external consumers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Breaking CLI contract change: the --category/-c thor option was removed from the Disqus importer, so existing invocations passing -c fail on Thor's unknown-option check and imported topics silently lose category assignment and original created_at preservation; the importer also switched to live-fetching thread URLs via TopicEmbed.import_remote, silently skipping dead or non-http links instead of importing them

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Thor option `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, so existing invocations using `-c/--category` will now fail Thor’s option parsing (unknown option). The importer logic also no longer computes/passes `category` or `created_at` into `PostCreator` (the old `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` is deleted) and instead calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which does not preserve the original `created_at` or category assignment shown in the previous code path. The additional claim about “silently skipping dead links” is not fully verifiable (open-uri failures would likely raise), but the breaking CLI contract and loss of metadata are directly evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Anonymous users can make the forum scrape and publish arbitrary pages of the embeddable host — the embed controller enqueues retrieve_topic with a fully user-controlled embed_url before any validation, and the job only checks URI(embed_url).host == embeddable_host leaving the path unrestricted, bypassing all posting permissions/trust levels by publishing as the configured embed_by_username user; the 60s throttle is per-URL so unlimited distinct URLs also flood sidekiq and hammer the host

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows unauthenticated access to `EmbedController#best` (no auth guard) which, when no existing `TopicEmbed` is found, enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` with `params[:embed_url]` (user-controlled) (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only verifies `URI(@embed_url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and does not constrain path/query (lib/topic_retriever.rb), so any URL under that host can be fetched server-side via `open(url)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). The import creates/updates posts as the configured `embed_by_username` user and uses `skip_validations: true` and `cook_method: :raw_html` (TopicEmbed.import + Post.cook change), effectively bypassing normal posting validation gates. Throttling is keyed by full URL (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so many distinct URLs can bypass the 60s throttle and flood Sidekiq / hammer the host (lib/topic_retriever.rb). While the controller does validate the *referer host* in `ensure_embeddable`, it does not validate that `embed_url` corresponds to the referer, so the abuse path remains.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs: //cdn.example.com/img.png matches start_with?('/'), gets its leading slashes stripped and is prefixed with the embed host producing http://blog.example.com/cdn.example.com/img.png; plain relative URLs (foo.html) are also left un-absolutized and break in the embedded context despite the method's stated contract

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, both `` and `` URLs are rewritten only when `href/src.start_with?('/')` and then `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips *all* leading slashes before prefixing with `#{prefix}/...`. This will mis-handle protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.png` by turning them into `http(s):///cdn.example.com/img.png`. Also, truly relative paths like `foo.html` are not rewritten at all despite the method comment stating it converts “any relative URLs to absolute”, which can break embedded rendering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embed resolution requires byte-exact match between the page URL and the feed link — topic_id_for_embed does exact string matching between the embed_url query param and the stored embed_url, so any divergence (trailing slash, scheme, or query params like FeedBurner's utm_source=feedburner) means the embed never resolves and the iframe shows the loading page forever, reloading every 30s and re-enqueueing retrieval every 60s with no error surfaced

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` does an exact string lookup (`where(embed_url: embed_url)`), with no URL normalization (scheme/host casing, trailing slash, query params). That can cause the same page to not match an existing `topic_embeds` row and trigger unnecessary retrieval and/or duplicate topics (since `TopicEmbed.import` stores `embed_url` exactly as passed). However, the finding’s claim that the embed "never resolves" and "shows the loading page forever" is not strictly supported by the diff: when no match is found, a `retrieve_topic` job is enqueued and `TopicRetriever` will eventually call `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)`, which would create a new `topic_embeds` row for the exact requested URL, allowing future resolution. So the core exact-match concern is valid, but the “forever” failure mode is overstated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: One malformed feed item permanently wedges the hourly feed import — rss.items.each calls TopicEmbed.import with no per-item error handling and the job sets retry: false, so a single item with nil title/content, a duplicate link (unique index on embed_url causing RecordNotUnique), or any import exception aborts the loop and every subsequent hourly run crashes at the same item, silently skipping everything after it forever

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the code iterates `rss.items.each` and calls `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and `TopicEmbed.import(...)` with no per-item `rescue`/error handling. A single bad item can raise (e.g., `i.content` being `nil` will raise `NoMethodError` on `.scrub`; `open(...)`/parsing can also raise), aborting the whole job before later items are processed. Because the scheduled job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, that failure won’t be retried automatically, so the hourly job can keep failing on subsequent runs until the feed/item changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: content_sha1 is advanced even when the revision didn't apply — embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...) runs regardless of whether revise! actually revised (it can return false or be aborted by a before_save callback), so once the sha1 is advanced changed content is never re-imported on later polls; the bypass_rate_limiter: true opt passed to PostRevisor has no corresponding handling in the code and is silently ignored

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing embed’s content changes, it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` and then unconditionally runs `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` (no check on whether the revision actually succeeded/applied). Since `PostRevisor#revise!` can return `false` (it explicitly does `return false if not should_revise?`), this can advance `content_sha1` even when the post was not updated, preventing future polls from retrying the import because the sha1s will now match. The note about `bypass_rate_limiter: true` being ignored is not fully verifiable from the diff alone because the full `PostRevisor` implementation isn’t shown, but the sha1-advancement issue is directly evidenced in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js postMessage origin check is substring-prefix based — discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 accepts any origin that is a string prefix of the forum URL (e.g., a forum at http://discourse.example.com accepts messages from http://discourse.example.co), enabling iframe-height manipulation as a clickjacking assist; the check should compare e.origin against the forum's exact origin

adjudication.rationale: In newly added app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, the message handler validates the sender with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. This is a substring check against the configured forum URL, so an origin that is a prefix of `discourseUrl` (e.g., `http://discourse.example.co` vs `http://discourse.example.com/`) will pass. That allows a non-forum origin to send `discourse-resize` messages and manipulate the embedded iframe height, which is a real security/clickjacking-assist issue in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true in create_table migrations silently drops an existing table and its data if the migration executes where the table already exists, and retroactively editing the already-released create_top_topics migration has no effect on databases that already applied it, diverging schema.rb-vs-migrations environments

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `force: true` to `create_table :topic_embeds` (new migration `20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb`) and retroactively changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` (`20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`). In Rails, `force: true` will drop an existing table before recreating it, which is a risky, potentially destructive behavior if the table already exists when the migration runs. Also, modifying an already-existing migration file means databases that have already applied that migration will not re-run it, so the change only affects fresh installs / new DBs, creating inconsistent behavior expectations across environments. This is a concrete, diff-grounded migration-safety concern, though it may not manifest as a defect in the typical migration path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Referer header is the only authorization gate for the embed endpoint — browsers/privacy settings that suppress Referer produce URI('').host == nil leading to a 403, so the embed silently never loads for those visitors with no fallback (e.g., signed/tokenized embed URL) and an invisible failure mode for both the embedding site and the forum operator

adjudication.rationale: The new embed endpoint is gated solely by `request.referer` host matching `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` (it raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` when `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`). If the Referer header is missing/suppressed, `URI('')` yields a nil host and the request is rejected; the controller spec even asserts failure when there is no referer. The finding’s core point (no fallback mechanism such as a signed/tokenized embed URL) is a valid diff-grounded product/edge-case concern, but it’s not a clear defect since the referer check appears to be an intentional security design choice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: the raw_html cook method makes cooked byte-identical to unsanitized raw, which Discourse renders with raw everywhere (embed view and normal topic views); feed item content never passes through any sanitizer and poll_feed.rb even calls CGI.unescapeHTML, converting entity-escaped <script> tags in feeds back into live tags, so a malicious/compromised feed or embeddable host yields stored XSS executing for every viewer including staff

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `:raw_html` cook method in `Post#cook` that returns `raw` byte-identical (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and sets `raw` to HTML derived from untrusted remote sources (RSS via `Jobs::PollFeed` and arbitrary URLs via `TopicEmbed.import_remote`). In `poll_feed.rb`, `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` can turn entity-escaped tags back into live HTML, and that content is persisted without any sanitizer. The embed view then renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so a malicious/compromised feed or embeddable host can store executable HTML/JS that will run for viewers.

matched_golden_ids: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unescaped request.referer is interpolated into an inline JavaScript string in app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — the ensure_embeddable host check constrains only the host, not path/query, so a crafted URL on an embeddable host breaks out of the JS string causing XSS on the Discourse origin with the viewer's cookies in scope; needs j/JSON encoding
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

It further explains the host check limitation, but the underlying vulnerability matches the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: External fetches have no timeout, size limit, or error handling — open-uri defaults in poll_feed.rb and topic_embed.rb leave ~60s+ per socket operation and unbounded read body size, so a slow or huge feed/page blocks Sidekiq workers for minutes or exhausts memory, and any SocketError/Timeout/parse error propagates as an unhandled job failure

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces external HTTP fetches using open-uri with no explicit timeouts, size limits, or exception handling. In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` can block on slow/never-responding feeds and will raise network/parse exceptions that aren’t rescued. In `app/models/topic_embed.rb#import_remote`, `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` reads the entire remote body unbounded and likewise has no timeout/limits/rescue. These code paths run in Sidekiq jobs (`Jobs::PollFeed`, `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` via `TopicRetriever`), so they can tie up workers and fail jobs on common network errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Throttle key is acquired before the fetch in lib/topic_retriever.rb — retrieved_recently? sets the 60s redis key before perform_retrieve runs, so if the fetch fails the job's first Sidekiq retry lands inside the throttle window, does nothing, and 'succeeds', ending the retry chain; transient failures are never effectively retried and recovery depends on new pageviews after 60s

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb`, `retrieve` calls `perform_retrieve` only if `retrieved_recently?` is false. But `retrieved_recently?` sets the Redis throttle key (`$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` then `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`) *before* `perform_retrieve` runs. If `perform_retrieve` (or downstream `open(...)` calls in `Jobs::PollFeed` / `TopicEmbed.import_remote`) raises due to a transient failure, a Sidekiq retry within 60s will hit `retrieved_recently? == true`, skip `perform_retrieve`, and return successfully—ending the retry chain while the throttle key is still active.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Every retrieval synchronously re-polls the entire feed — Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) runs the full feed fetch and import inline inside the retrieve_topic job, so any exception while polling propagates and skips fetch_http, meaning one broken feed item breaks on-demand embedding for every URL site-wide and is re-attempted on each job retry

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline (synchronously) before `fetch_http`, and there is no rescue around it. Any exception from `PollFeed#poll_feed` (e.g., `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` or `SimpleRSS.parse`) will bubble up and prevent `fetch_http` from running, so a broken/unreachable feed can block on-demand embedding for unrelated `@embed_url`s. Since `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` does not disable retries, Sidekiq retries would repeat this behavior each attempt.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No nil/validation guards on feed items in poll_feed.rb — i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError when an item lacks content, a nil i.title blows up topic creation, and URI(url) in TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls raises on feeds with unencoded spaces in links; the exception aborts the items loop and with retry: false a single persistent malformed item permanently blocks import of every item after it in the feed
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly flags that `i.content.scrub` can raise when a feed item lacks `content` (i.e., `i.content` is nil), which is the same core issue as the golden comment. It doesn’t explicitly mention falling back to `description`, but it identifies the same nil-crash risk in the same call site.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed rows are never cleaned up when topics/posts are deleted (no dependent/destroy hooks) — a stale row makes topic_id_for_embed return a dead id so TopicView.new raises, causing permanent 404/500 for that embed URL with no re-enqueued retrieval, and the update path crashes on PostRevisor.new(nil) when embed.post is nil

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces TopicEmbed records (with non-null topic_id/post_id and unique embed_url) but provides no cleanup mechanism when the associated Topic/Post is deleted: TopicEmbed only has `belongs_to :topic` / `belongs_to :post` with no `dependent:` behavior shown anywhere. `EmbedController#best` uses `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` and if it returns an id it unconditionally does `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` and does NOT enqueue retrieval; a stale TopicEmbed row pointing at a deleted topic would therefore prevent re-retrieval and can cause errors. Likewise, `TopicEmbed.import`’s update path does `post = embed.post` and then `PostRevisor.new(post)` if content changed; if the post was deleted, `embed.post` is nil and this will crash. These failure modes are directly implied by the added code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unauthenticated embed endpoint enqueues a background job per request with no throttle or input cap — the Referer check is trivially forged, there is no per-IP/route rate limit, no dedup, and no length limit on the embed_url param (job args go straight into redis), so combined with the 30s reload loop in loading.html.erb this is a Sidekiq/redis flooding vector

adjudication.rationale: The new unauthenticated `GET /embed/best` endpoint enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` returns nil, with no rate-limit/dedup before enqueue and no cap on `params[:embed_url]` size (EmbedController#best). Although `TopicRetriever` applies a 60s throttle per `embed_url` and checks for existing `TopicEmbed` (so there is some dedup/throttle at execution time), those protections happen *inside the job* and do not prevent an attacker from flooding Sidekiq/Redis with large numbers of queued jobs (and large `embed_url` payloads) by sending repeated requests with a forged `Referer` matching `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (ensure_embeddable only compares `URI(request.referer).host`). The 30s reload loop in `loading.html.erb` can also amplify repeated requests when an embed isn't yet available.

adjudication_records.issue_text: String#scrub requires Ruby 2.1+ but Ruby 2.0 was in use at the time and the string-scrub backport is not bundled in this PR — calling it in poll_feed.rb would be a NoMethodError breaking all feed polling

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a call to `String#scrub` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` (`content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`). However, the claim that the project was on Ruby 2.0 at the time (and that no backport is bundled) is not verifiable from this diff alone. What *is* diff-grounded is a potential runtime-compatibility risk: if `scrub` is not available in the deployed Ruby/stdlib set, feed polling would raise `NoMethodError` and fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic setnx/expire throttle in lib/topic_retriever.rb — if the process dies between setnx and expire the key has no TTL and that embed URL is permanently throttled (never retrieved again); should be a single SET with EX/NX

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, throttling does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. This is non-atomic; if the process dies/crashes after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will be left without a TTL, causing `setnx` to fail forever and the URL to be permanently treated as “retrieved recently” (throttled indefinitely). Using a single atomic `SET` with `NX` and `EX` would avoid this failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true in create_table migrations (create_topic_embeds.rb and the edit to already-shipped create_top_topics.rb) silently DROPs the table and its data if it already exists, and editing an already-released migration means existing installs never see the change

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `force: true` to `create_table` in a new migration (`db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb`) and also edits an existing migration (`db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`) to use `force: true`. In Rails, `create_table ..., force: true` will drop an existing table before creating it, which can cause data loss if the table already exists (e.g., partial/failed runs, manual table creation, or other environments). Additionally, modifying an already-existing migration means instances that already ran it will not receive this change via normal `db:migrate`, matching the finding’s point about existing installs not seeing the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent failure paths with no logging anywhere in the pipeline — topic_retriever.rb silently returns when the embed_by_username user is missing and topic_embed.rb silently returns for non-http URLs, so when embedding doesn't work jobs 'succeed' while doing nothing with no log or error to diagnose it

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows multiple early-return paths that do nothing without emitting any log/error: `TopicEmbed.import` returns immediately unless `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` (silent nil), and `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` returns if the configured `embed_by_username` doesn’t resolve to a user (`return if user.blank?`). adjudication_records.issue_text: Referer-based gating breaks for referer-suppressing clients — browsers/privacy settings/referrerpolicy that omit the Referer fail the host check and get 403 forever with no fallback, so the embed silently never loads for those users

adjudication.rationale: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` hard-requires a matching `request.referer` host: `raise ... if URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. If the browser/client omits the Referer header (privacy settings / referrerpolicy / some proxies), `request.referer` is nil, `URI('')` has `host == nil`, and the request is always rejected with InvalidAccess. There is no fallback to validate via the required `embed_url` param (even though `best` does `params.require(:embed_url)`), so the embed can never load for those clients.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 closes the header conditional with `<%- end if %>`, which ERB compiles to the Ruby statement `end if` — a syntax error (it should be `<%- end %>`); every request to /embed/best for a topic with posts raises ActionView::Template::Error and returns a 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:56-77 — absolutize_urls mishandles protocol-relative URLs: '//cdn.example.com/a.png' matches start_with?('/') and then has all leading slashes stripped by sub(/^\/+/, ''), producing http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/a.png — silently broken images/links.

Protocol-relative URLs like "//cdn.example.com/a.png" and "//cdn.example.com/a" also start with '/', so they will be rewritten to something like "http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/a.png" (prefix is based on the article host) after stripping both leading slashes. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:56-77 — absolutize_urls edge cases are untested: non-standard ports and the 'already-absolute URLs stay untouched' invariant are unpinned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — `<%- end if %>` is a Ruby syntax error; ERB passes `end if` through verbatim so the template cannot compile, raising ActionView::Template::Error and returning a 500 on every /embed/best request that finds a topic (the feature's success path); controller specs never render views so the suite can't catch it. adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: external feed HTML is imported and rendered with zero sanitization — app/models/post.rb:133 makes `cook` return `raw` verbatim for raw_html posts, bypassing the markdown/sanitize pipeline, while app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35-36 feeds `i.content` straight from the configured RSS/Atom feed into TopicEmbed.import → PostCreator (skip_validations: true, cook_method: raw_html), rendered with `raw post.cooked` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 and on the regular topic page — a malicious or compromised feed can store <script>/onerror= payloads executed for every visitor

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a code path where untrusted HTML is persisted and rendered without sanitization. `Post#cook` now returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == :raw_html` (app/models/post.rb), and `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). The scheduled feed job pulls `i.content` from an external RSS/Atom feed and passes it into `TopicEmbed.import` with only `CGI.unescapeHTML`/`scrub` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), i.e., no HTML sanitization. The embed view renders it using `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), and since `post.cooked == post.raw` for raw_html posts, this is a stored XSS vector if the feed is malicious/compromised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 interpolates the feed-supplied `url` into the 'imported from' HTML unescaped, allowing injection from the same untrusted feed source

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, it appends `"#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")}"` to `contents` with the feed/remote-supplied `url` interpolated directly into an HTML attribute and text without escaping. The only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes or other characters that can break out of the `href` attribute (e.g., `http://host/' onmouseover='...`). Since imported posts are created with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly, this HTML will be rendered unsanitized (e.g., via `raw post.cooked` in `embed/best.html.erb`), making this a verifiable XSS/injection risk from untrusted feed content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:47-52 whitelists `href` with no scheme check, so `javascript:` URLs survive absolutize_urls (lines 60-66 only rewrite leading-/ paths)

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import_remote, Readability::Document is configured to keep tags including `a`/`img` and allow attributes `%w[href src]` (no scheme filtering). The resulting `doc.content` is then imported with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and Post#cook returns `raw` unchanged for raw_html, while the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls only rewrites `href`/`src` that start with `/`, so `href="javascript:..."` (or other dangerous schemes) would remain intact and be rendered, enabling XSS in embedded content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` drops any pre-existing topic_embeds table before creating the new one; destructive DDL with no data safety that silently loses data in environments where an earlier iteration of the table exists, and rollback cannot restore the dropped data. A brand-new table needs no `force`

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which in Rails will drop an existing `topic_embeds` table before re-creating it. Since this is a table-creation migration for a new feature, `force: true` is unnecessary and introduces a real data-loss risk in any environment where the table already exists (e.g., a prior iteration or a partially-applied schema).

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — editing an already-committed migration to add `force: true`: deployed databases have already run it and will never see the edit, the added force flag silently drops existing top_topics data on any DB where the table exists but the version isn't recorded, and modifying shipped migrations produces divergent histories with pure destructive risk and no benefit

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. Adding `force: true` makes the migration drop and recreate the table if it already exists when this migration is executed, which is a concrete data-loss risk in any environment where `top_topics` exists but this migration hasn’t been recorded/applied. adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — NOT NULL + default on `posts` triggers a full table rewrite on PostgreSQL < 11 while holding an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, blocking all reads/writes on the app's largest table for the rewrite duration; safer to add the column nullable without default, backfill, then change_column to NOT NULL

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` (db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb). On PostgreSQL versions prior to 11, adding a column with a non-NULL default can rewrite the entire table and take an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, which is a significant operational risk for the large `posts` table. This is a valid, diff-grounded concern about deployment safety rather than an application correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb — no cleanup when an embedded topic/post is deleted: orphaned TopicEmbed rows make topic_id_for_embed return a stale id, /embed/best builds a TopicView for a deleted topic, and the next poll calls PostRevisor.new(nil) and crashes — with retry: false the exception aborts the items.each loop, so one orphaned embed halts the entire hourly feed import until manual cleanup

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds TopicEmbed without any dependent cleanup or foreign-key constraints. TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed simply plucks :topic_id, so an orphaned row can return an ID for a deleted topic; EmbedController#best then calls TopicView.new(topic_id, ...) with no guard. More critically, TopicEmbed.import assumes embed.post exists: in the update path it does `post = embed.post` and then `PostRevisor.new(post)` when the content changes. If the associated post was deleted but the TopicEmbed row remains, `embed.post` is nil and this will raise, aborting the RSS `rss.items.each` loop in Jobs::PollFeed (which has `sidekiq_options retry: false`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — no error handling: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every item has a content field, so plain RSS 2.0 feeds carrying only `description` raise NoMethodError; with no rescue anywhere and retry: false such feeds silently never import anything (hourly failures in sidekiq logs only), and any single malformed item aborts the loop, skipping all subsequent items

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` for each `rss.items` entry. If `i.content` is `nil` (e.g., feeds that only provide `description`), calling `.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the entire `rss.items.each` loop and preventing subsequent items from importing. There is no per-item rescue/handling in the job, and `sidekiq_options retry: false` means failures won’t be retried automatically, so the import can repeatedly fail on each hourly run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:37 — `content_sha1` is updated via update_column even if revisor.revise! failed to save, so a failed revision is recorded as 'in sync' and never retried, permanently diverging the topic from the source

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, when an existing embed’s content changes, it unconditionally runs `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` immediately after `revisor.revise!(...)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb, else branch). `PostRevisor#revise!` ultimately calls `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` and does not check the return value (lib/post_revisor.rb). If the save returns false (possible even with validations skipped, e.g., callbacks/DB issues that don’t raise), the SHA1 will still be updated, incorrectly marking the embed as synchronized and preventing future retries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:60-66 — absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs: `//cdn.example.com/img.png` starts with `/` and is rewritten to `http://host/cdn.example.com/img.png`, injecting a broken link/image into imported posts

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, both links and images are rewritten whenever the attribute starts_with?('/'). Protocol-relative URLs like "//cdn.example.com/img.png" also satisfy this condition, and href.sub(/^\/+/, '') strips both leading slashes, yielding "cdn.example.com/img.png". The code then rewrites it to "#{prefix}/cdn.example.com/img.png" (e.g., "http://host/cdn.example.com/img.png"), which is a broken URL. This is a concrete, diff-grounded correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117,141 — the `:category` option was removed, so existing documented invocations using `-c` are no longer accepted

adjudication.rationale: The diff in lib/tasks/disqus.thor removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` and the related `category_id` handling, replacing topic creation with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)`.
