adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117,141 — `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` was dropped in favor of scraping via TopicEmbed.import_remote, so imported topics lose their original timestamps (data fidelity loss) and topic creation additionally fails whenever the thread's page is unreachable or unparseable

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the prior `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) ...)` call is removed and replaced with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` fetches and parses the remote page via `open(url).read` and does not pass any `created_at` into `PostCreator` inside `TopicEmbed.import`, so imported posts/topics will get the current timestamp rather than the original `t[:created_at]`. Also, because `open(url).read`/Readability parsing are not wrapped in any rescue, an unreachable/unparseable thread URL will raise and can abort the import rather than still creating a placeholder topic/post as before.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: the `raw_html` cook method (`app/models/post.rb:131-133`) returns raw content verbatim, skipping the markdown pipeline, Sanitize, and `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook)` so plugin-added protections silently don't run; the RSS path (`poll_feed.rb:31`) runs `i.content` through `CGI.unescapeHTML` (re-arming entity-escaped `

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `raw_html` cook method where `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim (app/models/post.rb), bypassing the normal cooking pipeline and `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. New import paths explicitly set `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (TopicEmbed.import via PostCreator) and render via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), so any HTML in imported content is treated as safe. The RSS polling job decodes entities with `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), which can turn escaped tags into live markup before storage. Additionally, TopicEmbed.import interpolates `url` directly into a single-quoted `<a href='#{url}'>` footer without escaping (app/models/topic_embed.rb); the only validation is `^https?://`, which does not prevent quote-breaking payloads. The readability import only whitelists tag/attribute names (href/src) without any visible URI-scheme sanitization, so `javascript:` links in doc.content would survive and be rendered as raw HTML.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Poison-item cascade in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:27-33`: `rss.items.each` has no per-item error handling, so any exception aborts the run mid-iteration — e.g. nil `i.content` (SimpleRSS exposes `content:encoded` underscored) causing `nil.scrub` NoMethodError, a stale embed whose post was deleted crashing `PostRevisor.new(nil)` at `topic_embed.rb:30`, or `URI()` raising inside `absolutize_urls`; with `sidekiq_options retry: false` the next hourly run dies at the same item, permanently and silently halting all feed importing, and `topic_retriever.rb:37` invoking `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously per embed request compounds the failure

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop `rss.items.each do |i|` performs several operations that can raise (`i.content.scrub` if `i.content` is nil; `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`; `TopicEmbed.import(...)` which can raise from `URI(url)` in `absolutize_urls` or from `PostRevisor.new(post)` if `embed.post` is nil). There is no per-item rescue, so a single bad feed item aborts the whole job mid-iteration. Since `sidekiq_options retry: false` is set, that run will not be retried, and the same problematic item can cause repeated hourly failures and prevent importing later items. Additionally, `lib/topic_retriever.rb` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously during embed retrieval, so such exceptions can also break that request path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `cook_method` is settable through `PostCreator` opts (`lib/post_creator.rb:216`) with no allow-list of callers — a mass-assignment escape hatch to the unsanitized-HTML path; if any controller passes request params through as opts, any user can post with `cook_method=2` and store arbitrary raw HTML (trivial stored XSS), so the knob must be restricted to internal importers

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new, powerful knob: `PostCreator#setup_post` now blindly applies `@opts[:cook_method]` to the post (`lib/post_creator.rb`), and `Post#cook` returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (new enum + early return in `app/models/post.rb`). That creates an unsanitized-HTML path intended for internal importers (e.g., `TopicEmbed.import` passes `cook_method: ...[:raw_html]`). However, the finding’s claim that “any controller passes request params through as opts” (making it trivially user-exploitable stored XSS) is not verifiable from this diff alone because no controller changes showing user-controlled `PostCreator` opts are included here. Still, adding an unrestricted option like this is a concrete, diff-grounded security/architecture concern that should be constrained to trusted callers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host validation is scheme/port-blind and redirect-blind, enabling SSRF probing from the Discourse server (`lib/topic_retriever.rb:15`, `app/models/topic_embed.rb:42`): `invalid_host?` compares only `URI(@embed_url).host`, so `http://<embeddable_host>:6379/` and `ftp://` URLs pass the guard and are fetched by `open(url)` (open-uri supports FTP; the `^https?://` check in `import` runs only after the fetch), and open-uri following redirects lets an open redirect on the embeddable host make the server fetch internal/metadata URLs whose content is stored and readable back via the embed endpoint

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only compares `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` to `URI(@embed_url).host` (lib/topic_retriever.rb), ignoring scheme and port. If an attacker supplies an `embed_url` like `ftp://<embeddable_host>/...` or `http://<embeddable_host>:6379/...`, it will pass the host guard and reach `fetch_http`, which calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` performs `open(url).read` before any `^https?://` validation (that check exists only in `TopicEmbed.import` and runs after the fetch), so the server may fetch non-HTTP(S) URLs or unexpected ports. This is a real SSRF/probing risk introduced by the new embed retrieval code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unauthenticated, unthrottled Sidekiq job enqueue (queue-flooding DoS) at `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15`: the only gate on `GET /embed/best` is the client-controlled, trivially spoofable `Referer` header, and the 60s throttle lives inside the job, so every request with an unknown `embed_url` enqueues a `retrieve_topic` job plus a DB lookup at unbounded rate, flooding the shared Sidekiq queue and delaying legitimate work site-wide

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, it unconditionally enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` for every request (`app/controllers/embed_controller.rb`, new file). The only access gate shown is `ensure_embeddable`, which trusts `request.referer` host equality (`URI(request.referer||'').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`) and sets `X-Frame-Options = ALLOWALL`; `Referer` is a client-supplied header and can be trivially spoofed by non-browser clients. The 60s throttle is implemented inside `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` (in `lib/topic_retriever.rb`) and is only applied when the job runs, not before enqueue, so an attacker can flood Sidekiq with `retrieve_topic` jobs plus repeated DB lookups by issuing many GETs with a spoofed referer and varying `embed_url` values.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Exact-string URL keying with no normalization (`app/models/topic_embed.rb:11, 71`, `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:10`): `embed_url` is matched by exact string equality everywhere (lookup, unique index, throttle key), so trailing-slash, scheme (http/https), `www`, or query-param (`utm_*`) differences between the feed's `link` and the page's `discourseEmbedUrl` produce duplicate topics/discussions or a lookup that never hits, leaving the client reloading `loading.html.erb` every 30s forever while jobs keep being enqueued

adjudication.rationale: The diff keys embeds strictly by the raw `embed_url` string with no canonicalization: `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and `topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), unique DB index on `embed_url` (migration), controller lookup `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` and job enqueue uses the same string (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb), and throttling uses `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` (lib/topic_retriever.rb). This means semantically-identical URLs that differ by trailing slash, scheme, www, or tracking query params will be treated as distinct, allowing duplicate topics/embeds and bypassing the throttle. This is directly verifiable from the exact-equality queries and string-based keys in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `setnx`/`expire` in `lib/topic_retriever.rb:25-26` are not atomic: a crash between them leaves a TTL-less `retrieved:<url>` key, so that URL is considered 'recently retrieved' forever and is never imported (stuck on loading); should use a single atomic SET with EX

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle key is created with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then TTL is applied via a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. This is not atomic; if the process crashes or errors between the two calls, the key can be left without an expiry. Since subsequent calls will see `setnx` fail and return `true` (treated as "retrieved recently"), the embed URL can be permanently throttled and never retrieved/imported, leaving the embed stuck in the loading state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No terminal failure state and silent failures (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:8-10`, `lib/topic_retriever.rb:45-46`): the loading view reloads every 30s indefinitely, `fetch_http` silently returns when the `embed_by_username` user is missing, and failed fetches (404 page, blocked UA, empty readability result) are never logged or surfaced — misconfigured instances show an infinite 'Loading Discussion…' with zero diagnostics

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an embed loading flow with no failure/timeout path: `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` always reloads every 30s (`setTimeout(... document.location.reload() ...)`) and never transitions to an error state. In `lib/topic_retriever.rb#fetch_http`, if the configured `embed_by_username` user cannot be found (`return if user.blank?`), the retrieval is abandoned without creating a `TopicEmbed` and without surfacing any error, causing the embed endpoint (`EmbedController#best`) to keep rendering the loading view indefinitely. adjudication_records.issue_text: `force: true` in `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:4` silently drops any pre-existing table if the migration is re-run (redo, out-of-sync `schema_migrations`), and editing the already-released `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:2` means DBs that ran the original never see the change and diverge from fresh installs

adjudication_records.issue_text: `<%- end if %>` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6` works only by accident: ERB compiles it to `end if`, which Ruby parses as a modifier-if whose condition is the next statement Erubis emits (always truthy), so it renders correctly today purely by that accident — any adjacent template edit or different ERB compiler silently changes the condition or breaks compilation; should be `<%- end %>`

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, the conditional started with `<%- if @topic_view.posts.present? %>` is closed with `<%- end if %>` even though no condition follows `if`. This generates questionable Ruby (`end if ...`) and is at best dependent on how the ERB/Erubis compiler concatenates subsequent emitted code; it can lead to syntax/semantics changes or breakage with minor template edits. It should be a plain `<%- end %>` to correctly close the `if` block.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `disqus.thor` behavior regressions (`lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117-146`): the `category` and `created_at` options were removed so imported topics lose category and original timestamps, threads whose links aren't http(s) or whose live fetch fails are now silently skipped where they previously always imported, and `import_remote` makes a live HTTP request per thread

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `:category` option entirely (`lib/tasks/disqus.thor` deletes `method_option :category`) and stops passing both `created_at` and `category` into `PostCreator` (old code built `PostCreator.new(..., created_at: ..., category: category_id)`). It now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`.import` have no handling for category or created_at, so imported topics will no longer preserve category selection or original timestamps. Also, `TopicEmbed.import` returns early unless `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, so threads with non-http(s) `t[:link]` will result in `post` being nil and the thread effectively skipped (the thor task only continues when `post.present?`). Finally, `import_remote` does a live `open(url).read` per thread, increasing network dependency/cost compared to the previous permalink-only topic creation.
